The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped being collected
Why, in plain words: A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, but the monitoring was not changed to use the new label, so it stopped collecting them.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 6m 32s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #537 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped being collected while metrics.portName was http-metrics
Incident: MetricsAbsent on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:46 to 02:52:32 UTC, metrics missing until then
Status: Draft. 1 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 03:09:31 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:51:53 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
No metrics were collected from 02:46 UTC until they resumed at 02:52:32 UTC, 6 minutes 32 seconds later. The service's own logs reach into that stretch until 02:51 UTC, as far as they were read. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, but the monitoring was not changed to use the new label, so it stopped collecting them. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #537, for a person to review and merge. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). Any deploy of what the repository now holds could stop the shop's metrics again, and any later rename of the port in one deploy file but not the other could do the same.

Impact
6m 32s - onset until the metrics resumed
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: No metrics received from io-shop since 2026-11-11T02:46:00Z - 5m with no sample, against a scrape interval of 15 seconds. The series stopped rather than crossing a threshold, so nothing here says whether the shop is well: these minutes have no readings to judge, not readings that look bad.
The metrics stop at the onset, so the duration is how long they were missing, until they resumed - not a stretch the service is known to have spent broken.
The service's own logs reach into the stretch the metrics missed until 02:51 UTC: G46bc, Gbac1. They were read up to then. As far as they show, the service went on serving as it had before the metrics stopped.

Root cause and contributing factors
The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics endpoint by the port's name rather than its number, and the deploy renamed that port from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml without changing the scrape configuration, which it left as it was. The scraper's selector then matched no port and it had nothing to collect from, while nothing reported an error.
Causal chain
symptom Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and the monitoring went blind to the service.
  Evidence:
    AL1
    T4 02:52:15 Investigator Agent: Read the service's metrics - they stop after the minute at 02:45, and nothing covers the minutes since
    G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 4 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:44–02:45. After they stopped: 9 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:46–02:51
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:44–02:45; # was 1.50%. After they stopped: 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:46–02:51; # was 0.50% to 2.00%, typically 0.50%, highest at 02:51
why 1 The metrics stopped because of the deploy recorded at 02:46:07 UTC, which changed metrics.portName from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml. That was the only change in the deploy.
  Evidence:
    P2 02:46:07 UTC deploy 9f4ad14 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 9f4ad14 to io-shop, compared against e283ba3 - the revision deployed before it.
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision e283ba3: the shop's metrics were still being collected with it in place up to the minute before the onset, and they could be read again once the rollback put that revision back.
      T4
      M1 02:52:32 Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1: confirmed, still in place
      T18 02:53:06 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - its metrics could be read again from 02:52
      T19 02:53:06 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:52:26.
      T14
why 2 The rename stopped collection because the deploy left the scrape configuration unchanged, so the scrape no longer matched any port on the shop and had no target to collect from.
  Evidence:
    S1 deploy/values-production.yaml at 9f4ad14
    D1
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that makes the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml agree with the name the scrape configuration selects. The values file's own comment says the name carries weight and that a name nothing matches stops collection without any error. (AI-4)
- No check was seen after rollout that the scraper still had a target for the shop, so the deploy finished even though collection had stopped. (AI-5)
- The absent-metrics alert came 3 minutes 17 seconds later than its evaluation interval and scrape allowance account for, and the record does not show what took that time. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The service is still serving normally, but the metrics stopped. The deploy at 02:46:07 UTC changed one value, metrics.portName, from metrics to http-metrics in deploy/values-production.yaml. The scrape appears to select the port by name, so it can no longer find it. The rows stop at 02:45 UTC, and the logs keep answering normally afterwards. | 0.70 | confirmed
C2 | The deploy changed the configuration value metrics.portName, and that broke metrics exposure. This is the same change as the first hypothesis, read as a faulty config rather than a blind spot in the monitoring. | 0.15 | confirmed, as tested for C1
C3 | The deploy was a rename meant to apply a naming convention, and the scrape configuration was not updated to match. | 0.10 | confirmed, as tested for C1

Trigger
metrics.portName went from metrics to http-metrics at 02:46:07 UTC, in the deploy of 9f4ad14 that kuki started.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:52:32 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
 | 02:54:44 | Proposed a fix: PR #537 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The metrics on io-shop stopped at 02:46 UTC. MetricsAbsent fired at 02:51:47 UTC, 5 minutes 47 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #537 | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a required pre-merge check, run on every change to the deploy/ directory, that fails when metrics.portName in deploy/values-production.yaml differs from any port name the scrape configuration selects. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Add a post-deploy check to io-shop's rollout that fails the rollout when the scraper has no target for the shop. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Find out what took the 3 minutes 17 seconds by which the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop came later than its evaluation and scrape allowance account for, and remove it. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Route MetricsAbsent alerts on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when they fire. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 38 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 9f4ad14 changed.
- 45 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 1 minute 19 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent looked at the service - its metrics could be read again from 02:52.
- 2 minutes 57 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #537.
What went wrong
- The alert came 3 minutes 17 seconds later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the metrics' stopping is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
- Nobody was paged: the MetricsAbsent alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was called in while the shop's metrics were missing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Response effort
none - engineer time
139,725 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/37c20a0a-8fd3-4d27-96fc-c05b828d211c
The fix it proposed: PR #537 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/537) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
P1 | Nov 10, 2026, 22:46:07 UTC deploy e283ba3 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
P2 | 02:46:07 UTC deploy 9f4ad14 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
Flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 4 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:44–02:45. After they stopped: 9 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:46–02:51
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 2 occurrences in 2 minutes, 02:44–02:45; # was 1.50%. After they stopped: 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 02:46–02:51; # was 0.50% to 2.00%, typically 0.50%, highest at 02:51
What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 9f4ad14 to io-shop, compared against e283ba3 - the revision deployed before it.
modified deploy/values-production.yaml
  @@ -43,7 +43,7 @@ autoscaling:
   # the only sign is that the series stops.
   metrics:
     port: 9090
  -  portName: metrics
  +  portName: http-metrics
   
   # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
   #
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: deploy/scrape.yaml says it picks the endpoint to scrape by the port's name (endpoints: - port: metrics). Its own comment says that name has to match metrics.portName in deploy/values-production.yaml, and that nothing checks the two agree. A name that matches no port leaves Prometheus with no targets, and nothing reports an error. Deploy 9f4ad14 renamed the port to http-metrics in values-production.yaml but did not change scrape.yaml, so the selector matched nothing. That is why the metrics stopped while the service kept serving.

The fix: change the ServiceMonitor endpoint to port: http-metrics, so it matches the name the deploy now gives the port. The deploy stays in place, nothing is reverted.

The test: I added tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py to cover the missing check. It reads metrics.portName from values-production.yaml and every port: entry under the ServiceMonitor's endpoints in scrape.yaml, using plain line parsing so it needs no YAML library. It asserts that every scraped port name equals the configured portName. Against the current files it should fail ('metrics' vs 'http-metrics'). With this change it should pass, and it will catch the next rename that updates only one of the two files.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | deploy/values-production.yaml at 9f4ad14
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, the monitoring system stopped collecting io-shop's figures. Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, but the monitoring was not changed to use the new label, so it stopped collecting them. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. Argus ended the incident by rolling back the shop's deployment. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off. Argus has also proposed a fix, but it is only a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
